questions.q: What does the term 'Reproductive Health' primarily refer to?
options: The absence of diseases in reproductive organs
Healthy reproductive organs with normal functions
questions.solution: Reproductive Health simply refers to healthy reproductive organs with normal functions. Therefore, a society with people having physically and functionally normal reproductive organs and normal emotional and behavioural interactions among them in all sex-related aspects might be called reproductively healthy.

questions.q: In what year did India’s population cross the 1 billion mark?
questions.solution: In the last century an all-round development in various fields significantly improved the quality of life of the people. However, increased health facilities along with better living conditions had an explosive impact on the growth of population. The world population which was around 2 billion (2000 million) in 1900 rocketed to about 6 billion by 2000 and 7.2 billion in 2011. A similar trend was observed in India too. Our population which was approximately 350 million at the time of our independence reached close to the billion mark by 2000 and crossed 1.2 billion in May 2011. A rapid decline in death rate, maternal mortality rate (MMR) and infant mortality rate (IMR) as well as an increase in number of people in reproducible age are probable reasons for this. Through our Reproductive Child Health (RCH) programme, though we could bring down the population growth rate, it was only marginal.According to the 2011 census report, the population growth rate was less than 2 per cent, i.e., 20/1000/year, a rate at which our population could increase rapidly.

questions.q: What principle do natural methods of contraception work on?
options: Avoiding chances of ovum and sperm meeting
questions.solution: Natural methods work on the principle of avoiding chances of ovum and sperms meeting. Periodic abstinence is one such method in which the couples avoid or abstain from coitus from day 10 to 17 of the menstrual cycle when ovulation could be expected. As chances of fertilisation are very high during this period, it is called the fertile period. Therefore, by abstaining from coitus during this period, conception could be prevented. Withdrawal or coitus interruptus is another method in which the male partner withdraws his penis from the vagina just before ejaculation so as to avoid insemination. Lactational amenorrhea (absence of menstruation) method is based on the fact that ovulation and therefore the cycle do not occur during the period of intense lactation following parturition. Therefore, as long as the mother breast-feeds the child fully, chances of conception are almost nil. However, this method has been reported to be effective only upto a maximum period of six months following parturition. As no medicines or devices are used in these methods, side effects are almost nil. Chances of failure, though, of this method are also high.

questions.q: What material are condoms typically made from?
questions.solution: Condomsare barriers made of thin rubber/ latex sheath that are used to cover the penis in the male or vagina and cervix in the female, just before coitus so that the ejaculated semen would not enter into the female reproductive tract. This can prevent conception. ‘Nirodh’ is a popular brand of condom for the male. Use of condoms has increased in recent years due to its additional benefit of protecting the user from contracting STIs and AIDS. Both the male and the female condoms are disposable, can be self-inserted and thereby gives privacy to the user. Diaphragms, cervical caps and vaults are also barriers made of rubber that are inserted into the female reproductive tract to cover the cervix during coitus. They prevent conception by blocking the entry of sperms through the cervix. They are reusable. Spermicidal creams, jellies and foams are usually used alongwith these barriers to increase their contraceptive efficiency

questions.solution: Condoms are barriers made of thin rubber/ latex sheath that are used to cover the penis in the male or vagina and cervix in the female, just before coitus so that the ejaculated semen would not enter into the female reproductive tract. This can prevent conception. ‘Nirodh’ is a popular brand of condom for the male. Use of condoms has increased in recent years due to its additional benefit of protecting the user from contracting STIs and AIDS. Both the male and the female condoms are disposable, can be self-inserted and thereby gives privacy to the user. Diaphragms, cervical caps and vaults are also barriers made of rubber that are inserted into the female reproductive tract to cover the cervix during coitus. They prevent conception by blocking the entry of sperms through the cervix. They are reusable. Spermicidal creams, jellies and foams are usually used alongwith these barriers to increase their contraceptive efficiency

questions.q: Where are IntraUterine Devices (IUDs) inserted?
questions.solution: Another effective and popular method is the use of Intra Uterine Devices (IUDs). These devices are inserted by doctors or expert nurses in the uterus through vagina. IUDs are ideal contraceptives for the females who want to delay pregnancy and/or space children. It is one of most widely accepted methods of contraception in India.

questions.q: What do oral contraceptive pills contain?
questions.solution: Oral administration of small doses of either progestogens or progestogen–estrogen combinations is another contraceptive method used by the females. They are used in the form of tablets and hence are popularly called the pills. Pills have to be taken daily for a period of 21 days starting preferably within the first five days of menstrual cycle. After a gap of 7 days (during which menstruation occurs) it has to be repeated in the same pattern till the female desires to prevent conception. They inhibit ovulation and implantation as well as alter the quality of cervical mucus to prevent/retard entry of sperms. Pills are very effective with lesser side effects and are well accepted by the females. Saheli–the new oral contraceptive for the females contains a non-steroidal preparation. It is a ‘once a week’ pill with very few side effects and high contraceptive value.

questions.q: What are surgical methods of contraception also called?
questions.solution: Surgical methods, also called sterilisation, are generally advised for the male/female partner as a terminal method to prevent any more pregnancies. Surgical intervention blocks gamete transport and thereby prevent conception. Sterilisation procedure in the male is called ‘vasectomy’ and that in the female, ‘tubectomy’. In vasectomy, a small part of the vas deferens is removed or tied up through a small incision on the scrotum whereas in tubectomy, a small part of the fallopian tube is removed or tied up through a small incision in the abdomen or through vagina. These techniques are highly effective but their reversibility is very poor

questions.q: What is the term for the intentional or voluntary termination of pregnancy before full term?
questions.solution: Intentional or voluntary termination of pregnancy before full term is called medical termination of pregnancy (MTP) or induced abortion. Nearly 45 to 50 million MTPs are performed in a year all over the world which accounts to 1/5th of the total number of conceived pregnancies in a year. Whether to accept / legalise MTP or not is being debated upon in many countries due to emotional, ethical, religious and social issues involved in it. Government of India legalised MTP in 1971 with some strict conditions to avoid its misuse. Such restrictions are all the more important to check indiscriminate and illegal female foeticides which are reported to be high in India.

questions.solution: RCH work towards creating awareness among people about various reproduction related aspects and providing facilities and support for building up a reproductively healthy society.

Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: Teachers have a major role in creating awareness about reproduction related aspects
Reason: Introduction of sex education in schools should also be encouraged to provide right information to the young so as to discourage children from believing in myths and having misconceptions about sex-related aspects.
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution: Parents, other close relatives, teachers and friends, also have a major role in the dissemination of the above information. Introduction of sex education in schools should also be encouraged to provide right information to the young so as to discourage children from believing in myths and having misconceptions about sex-related aspects.
questions.subject: Zoology

questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: People in adolescent age should know proper information about reproductive organs
Reason: Proper knowledge about reproductive organs and STD is needed to lead a healthy life
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution: Proper information about reproductive organs, adolescence and related changes, safe and hygienic sexual practices, sexually transmitted diseases (STD), AIDS, etc., would help people, especially those in the adolescent age group to lead a reproductively healthy life.
questions.subject: Zoology

questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: Successful implementation of various action plans to attain reproductive health requires strong infrastructural facilities,
Reason: Infrastructural facilities are essential to provide medical assistance
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution: Successful implementation of various action plans to attain reproductive health requires strong infrastructural facilities, professional expertise and material support. These are essential to provide medical assistance and care to people in reproduction-related problems like pregnancy, delivery, STDs, abortions, contraception, menstrual problems, infertility, etc.
questions.subject: Zoology

questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: Statutory ban on sex determination through amniocentesis has been implemented
Reason: The ban has been implemented to legally check increasing menace of female foeticides

Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion

Both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution: Statutory ban on amniocentesis for sex-determination to legally check increasing menace of female foeticides, massive child immunisation, etc.
questions.subject: Zoology

Assertion: In amniocentesis some of the amniotic fluid is taken to analyse

Assertion: Better awareness about sex related disorders lead to decreased maternal and infant mortality rates
Reason: Awareness of sex related disorders lead to increased number of medically assisted deliveries

Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution: Better awareness about sex related matters, increased number of medically assisted deliveries and better post-natal care leading to decreased maternal and infant mortality rates.
questions.subject: Zoology

questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: World population rocketed from 2 billion in 1900 to 7.2 billion in 2011
Reason: In the last century an all-round development in various fields significantly improved the quality of life of the people.
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution: Increased health facilities along with better living conditions had an explosive impact on the growth of population. The world population which was around 2 billion (2000 million) in 1900 rocketed to about 6 billion by 2000 and 7.2 billion in 2011.
questions.subject: Zoology

questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: Government was forced to take up serious measures to check population growth
Reason: An alarming growth rate could lead to an absolute scarcity of even the basic requirements, i.e., food, shelter and clothing
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution: An alarming growth rate could lead to an absolute scarcity of even the basic requirements, i.e., food, shelter and clothing, in spite of significant progress made in those areas. Therefore, the government was forced to take up serious measures to check this population growth rate.
questions.subject: Zoology

questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: Incentives given to small families is a measure to overcome overpopulation
Reason: The most important step to overcome this problem is to motivate smaller families by using various contraceptive methods.
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution: Statutory raising of marriageable age of the female to 18 years and that of males to 21 years, and incentives given to couples with small families are two of the other measures taken to tackle the problem overpopulation.
questions.subject: Zoology

questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: A contraceptive should be user friendly and effective
Reason: Contraceptives can be grouped into categories like barrier, IUDs, oral contraceptives etc.
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution: An ideal contraceptive should be user-friendly, easily available, effective and reversible with no or least side-effects. It also should in no way interfere with the sexual drive, desire and/or the sexual act of the user.
questions.subject: Zoology

questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: Periodic abstinence is an example of natural method of contraception
Reason: As chances of fertilisation are very high during the period of day 10 to 17 of the menstrual cycle, it is called the fertile period
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution: Natural methods work on the principle of avoiding chances of ovum and sperms meeting. Periodic abstinence is one such method in which the couples avoid or abstain from coitus from day 10 to 17 of the menstrual cycle when ovulation could be expected.
questions.subject: Zoology

questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: Coitus interruptus is a type of natural contraceptive
Reason: Natural methods work on the principle of avoiding chances of ovum and sperms meeting
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution: Withdrawal or coitus interruptus is another method in which the male partner withdraws his penis from the vagina just before ejaculation so as to avoid insemination.
questions.subject: Zoology

questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: Chances of conception are nil during breast feeding by mother
Reason: This type of contraceptive measure has been reported to be effective only upto a maximum period of six months following parturition.
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution: Lactational amenorrhea (absence of menstruation) method is based on the fact that ovulation and therefore the cycle do not occur during the period of intense lactation following parturition. Therefore, as long as the mother breast-feeds the child fully, chances of conception are almost nil.
questions.subject: Zoology

questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: Condom is a type of barrier method of contraception
Reason: In barrier methods, ovum and sperms are prevented from physically meeting with the help of barriers.
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution: Condoms are barriers made of thin rubber/ latex sheath that are used to cover the penis in the male or vagina and cervix in the female, just before coitus so that the ejaculated semen would not enter into the female reproductive tract.
questions.subject: Zoology

questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: Diaphragms are female contraceptive barriers
Reason: Spermicidal creams, jellies and foams are usually used alongwith these barriers to reduce their contraceptive efficiency.
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution: Diaphragms, cervical caps and vaults are also barriers made of rubber that are inserted into the female reproductive tract to cover the cervix during coitus. They prevent conception by blocking the entry of sperms through the cervix.
questions.subject: Zoology

questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: IUDs supress sperm motility
Reason: IUDs are devices are inserted by doctors or expert nurses in the fallopian tubes through vagina.
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution: IUDs increase phagocytosis of sperms within the uterus and the Cu ions released suppress sperm motility and the fertilising capacity of sperms.
questions.subject: Zoology

questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: Pills have to be taken daily for a period of 21 days
Reason: Oral administration of small doses of either testosterone or testosterone–estrogen combinations is another contraceptive method used by the females.
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution: Pills have to be taken daily for a period of 21 days starting preferably within the first five days of menstrual cycle. After a gap of 7 days (during which menstruation occurs) it has to be repeated in the same pattern till the female desires to prevent conception.
questions.subject: Zoology

questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: Hormones can injected as a method of contraception
Reason: Saheli is a thrice a week pill
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution: Progestogens alone or in combination with estrogen can also be used by females as injections or implants under the skin. Their mode of action is similar to that of pills and their effective periods are much longer.
questions.subject: Zoology

questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: Vasectomy prevents release of sperms
Reason: Surgical intervention facilitates gamete transport and thereby prevent contraception.
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution: In vasectomy, a small part of the vas deferens is removed or tied up through a small incision on the scrotum that prevents the release of sperm.
questions.subject: Zoology

Reason: MTPs are considered unsafe during the the first semester
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution: MTPs are essential in certain cases where continuation of the pregnancy could be harmful or even fatal either to the mother or to the foetus or both.
questions.subject: Zoology

questions.q:

Reason: HIV can be transmitted by contact
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution: Infections or diseases which are transmitted through sexual intercourse are collectively called sexually transmitted infections (STI) or venereal diseases (VD) or reproductive tract infections (RTI).
questions.subject: Zoology

questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: Genital herpes is completely curable
Reason: Using condoms can lead to STIs
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution: Genital herpes and HIV infections, other diseases are completely curable if detected early and treated properly. Early symptoms of most of these are minor and include itching,fluid discharge, slight pain, swellings, etc., in the genital region. Infected females may often be asymptomatic and hence, may remain undetected for long.
questions.subject: Zoology

questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: Untimely detection of STIs could lead to pulmonary disease
Reason: Infection of STIs are high among age groups of 40-50 years
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution: Absence or less significant symptoms in the early stages of infection and the social stigma attached to the STIs, deter the infected persons from going for timely detection and proper treatment. This could lead to complications later, which include pelvic inflammatory diseases (PID), abortions, still births, ectopic pregnancies, infertility or even cancer of the reproductive tract.
questions.subject: Zoology

questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: Psycholgical factors do not affect infertility
Reason: Infertility clinics help to diagnose STIs
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution: The reasons for infertility could be many–physical, congenital, diseases, drugs, immunological or even psychological.
questions.subject: Zoology

Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.

Reason: In India male is more often blamed for being infertile

Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution: Couples could be assisted to have children through certain special techniques commonly known as assisted reproductive technologies (ART) when correction of reproductive disorders are not possible.
questions.subject: Zoology

Reason: IVF is an exclusively in vivo process
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution: In vitro fertilisation (IVF–fertilisation outside the body in almost similar conditions as that in the body) followed by embryo transfer (ET) is one of the methods of conception for infertile couples.
questions.subject: Zoology

questions.q:

Assertion: In embryo transfer, embryos with more than 8 blastomeres are transferred into fallopian tubes
Reason: Ovum from a donor cannot be transferred another female for conception
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false

questions.solution: Embryos with more than 8 blastomeres, into the uterus (IUT – intra uterine transfer), to complete its further development.
questions.subject: Zoology

Assertion: GIFT is a method to cure a female who cannot produce ovum
Reason: Embryos formed by in-vivo fertilisation (fusion of gametes within the female) cannot be used for such transfer to assist those females who cannot conceive
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution: Transfer of an ovum collected from a donor into the fallopian tube (GIFT – gamete intra fallopian transfer) of another female who cannot produce one, but can provide suitable environment for fertilisation and further development is another method attempted.
questions.subject: Zoology

Infertility cases either due to inability of the male partner to inseminate the female or due to very low sperm counts in the ejaculates, could be corrected by artificial insemination (AI) technique.
